explanation: For each keyword position retain its latest occurrence and the shortest covering-prefix length ending there. A match at position j extends the previous keyword state by the gap between occurrences. Check the result whenever the final keyword matches.
timeComplexity: O(n + k) expected time for n paragraph entries and k distinct keywords. Each paragraph word updates at most one state after O(k) keyword indexing. The entry-count bound treats word hashing/comparison as constant; include examined character lengths when words are unbounded.
spaceComplexity: O(k) auxiliary space. There are O(k) keyword indices and prefix states.

correctness: For each keyword prefix, the saved state represents the latest possible start of a valid occurrence sequence ending at its latest occurrence. Extending the preceding state adds exactly the index gap, preserving that start. A later valid start never hurts any future extension, so discarding older starts is safe. Checking each completion of the final keyword therefore finds a shortest interval.
walkthrough: For [elm,oak,cedar,elm,oak,ash,pine] and [elm,oak,ash], elm at 3 resets its prefix length to 1. Oak at 4 gets length 1+(4−3)=2. Ash at 5 gets length 2+(5−4)=3, so return inclusive interval (3,5). The wrapper observes length 3. The callable returns inclusive zero-based endpoints. The executable walkthrough expected value is their length after the wrapper checks the required keyword sequence.
edgeCases: Keywords are distinct and the supplied corpus guarantees a covering interval.
Repeated paragraph matches must allow a newer, shorter prefix to replace an older one.
A single keyword gives a one-entry interval; ties may use any shortest valid interval.
